degree_requirements.program: B.S. in Electrical and Computer Engineering (UW Seattle)

courses.title: Engineering Exploration
courses.description: Presentations and discussions on topics of current interest in engineering. Explores various areas of engineering research, engineering disciplines, and relevance to students.

courses.title: The University Community
courses.description: Introduces students to various aspects of the University of Washington community, university resources, opportunities, and academic skill development.

courses.title: Calculus with Analytic Geometry I
courses.description: Differential calculus, limits, continuity, definition of derivative, differentiation techniques, and applications.

courses.title: Calculus with Analytic Geometry II
courses.description: Integral calculus, definite integrals, integration techniques, applications, and introductory differential equations.

courses.title: Calculus with Analytic Geometry III
courses.description: Taylor series, vector geometry, parametric equations, and introductory multivariable calculus.

courses.title: Introduction to Differential Equations
courses.description: Ordinary differential equations, initial value problems, first- and second-order linear equations, and Laplace transforms.

courses.title: Introduction to Differential Equations and Applications
courses.description: Introductory survey of ordinary differential equations, linear and nonlinear equations, Taylor series, and Laplace transforms with science and engineering examples.

courses.title: Matrix Algebra with Applications
courses.description: Systems of linear equations, vector spaces, matrices, subspaces, orthogonality, least squares, eigenvalues, and eigenvectors.

courses.title: Applied Linear Algebra and Numerical Analysis
courses.description: Analysis and application of numerical methods and algorithms to problems in applied sciences and engineering using MATLAB or Python.

courses.title: Probability and Statistics for Engineers
courses.description: Application of probability theory and statistics to engineering problems, distribution theory, statistical inference, quality control, and linear regression.

courses.title: Statistical Methods in Engineering and Science
courses.description: Concepts of probability and statistics, conditional probability, random variables, sampling errors, confidence intervals, and least squares.

courses.title: General Chemistry I
courses.description: Atomic nature of matter, quantum mechanics, ionic and covalent bonding, molecular geometry, stoichiometry, solution stoichiometry, and gas laws.

courses.title: Mechanics
courses.description: Basic principles of mechanics and experiments in mechanics for physical science and engineering majors.

courses.title: Electromagnetism
courses.description: Basic principles of electromagnetism, electric fields, Gauss's law, circuits, magnetic fields, and electromagnetic induction.

courses.title: Waves, Light, and Heat
courses.description: Oscillations, waves, sound, geometric and wave optics, interference, diffraction, and thermodynamics.

courses.title: Introduction to Neuroscience
courses.description: Provides a broad introduction to the study of brain function, emphasizing how circuits within the brain process sensory information and generate movement.

courses.title: Introductory Biology
courses.description: Animal and plant physiology, comparative anatomy, transport, gas exchange, nutrition, and homeostasis.

courses.title: Advanced Multivariable Calculus
courses.description: Multivariate integration including double and triple integrals, vector fields, line and surface integrals, and theorems of Green, Stokes, and Gauss.

courses.title: Introduction to Computer Programming I
courses.description: Introduction to computer programming for students without previous programming experience using procedural constructs and control structures.

courses.title: Introduction to Computer Programming II
courses.description: Emphasizes program design, style, decomposition, and data structures like lists, dictionaries, and sets.

courses.title: Introduction to Computer Programming III
courses.description: Introduction to data abstraction, object-oriented programming, recursion, and implementation of core data structures.

courses.title: Computer Programming I
courses.description: Basic programming concepts, conditional execution, loops, methods, arrays, and objects.

courses.title: Computer Programming II
courses.description: Continuation of CSE 142. Core data structures, recursive programming, sorting, and searching.

courses.title: Intermediate Data Programming
courses.description: Intermediate programming concepts in Python, including data structures, file processing, data visualization, and tabular/geospatial data analysis.

courses.title: Computer Hardware Skills
courses.description: Introduction to computer hardware skills, soldering, circuit prototyping, and laboratory instrumentation.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering
courses.description: Basic circuit and systems concepts, Kirchhoff's laws, resistors, sources, capacitors, inductors, and operational amplifiers.

courses.title: Programming for Signal and Information Processing Applications
courses.description: Introduction to programming tailored for signal processing, numerical computation, and data manipulation in Python.

courses.title: Signals, Systems, and Data I
courses.description: Continuous- and discrete-time signals and systems, impulses, unit steps, convolution, and Fourier series and transforms.

courses.title: Digital Circuits and Systems
courses.description: Overview of digital computer systems, Boolean algebra, combinational and sequential circuits, logic design, and programmable logic devices.

courses.title: Exploring Devices
courses.description: Overview of modern electronic and photonic devices underlying modern electronic products, semiconductors, diodes, and transistors.

courses.title: Advanced Technical Communication
courses.description: Practical skills for day-to-day engineering communication and preparing persuasive documents and presentations for technical and non-technical audiences.
